LESSON: RHYTHM

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.2: Rhythm
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Rhythm, part of Creating and Performing in Grade 9 CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS.

Key inquiry question: How can various note combinations be used to form rhythms in simple time? 2. How can one improvise accompaniment patterns for Sports?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to, sing or play tunes involving dotted notes to outline effects of note extension in rhythmic patterns,

2. beat time to familiar tunes in 4 4 time considering the crochet as principle beat, accented and weak beats,

3. group notes of given two-bar rhythmic patterns involving dotted notes in 4 4 time,

4. orally compose 4-bar rhythmic patterns involving dotted notes and their corresponding rests, in 4 4 time and write on monotone,

5. write rhythmic patterns from dictation, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to, sing or play tunes involving dotted notes to outline effects of note extension in rhythmic patterns,
2. beat time to familiar tunes in 4 4 time considering the crochet as principle beat, accented and weak beats,
3. group notes of given two-bar rhythmic patterns involving dotted notes in 4 4 time,
4. orally compose 4-bar rhythmic patterns involving dotted notes and their corresponding rests, in 4 4 time and write on monotone,
5. write rhythmic patterns from dictation, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Rhythm together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: The learner, through effective communication, articulates and discusses the effect of

note extension in rhythmic patterns, with peers.

• Learning to Learn: The learner actively seeks to understand and apply notation conventions to represent rhythm in music.

• Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: The learner creatively solves problems related to achieving the desired solutions on

rhythmic structure in creating rhythmic patterns,

• Creativity and Imagination: The learner embraces creativity by exploring innovative factors such as unique combinations of

beats, or experimental rhythmic elements as they create rhythmic patterns.
